content: 1. Discard this product promptly when it has expired or is no longer needed. 2. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. 3. This document is a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. 4. This information does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. 5. This document is not a substitute for individualized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. 6. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: 7. Penicillin is an antibiotic used to treat and prevent a wide range of bacterial infections. 8. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: 9. Shake the bottle well before each dose. 10. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. Avoid using a household spoon, as it may not provide the correct dose. 11. This medication can be taken with or without food. 12. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. 13. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. 14. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: 15. Common side effects may include upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and mouth sores. 16. Rarely, you may develop a harmless black, hairy tongue while taking this medication. This effect usually resolves after treatment. 17. Maintain good oral hygiene and brush your tongue with a soft toothbrush twice daily. 18. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 19. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. 20. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (fungal infections). 21. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. Precautions: 22. Before taking penicillin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other penicillin-type antibiotics (e.g., amoxicillin, ampicillin), cephalosporins (e.g., cephalexin, cefuroxime), or any other allergies. 23. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. 24. This medication may contain aspartame. 25. Penicillin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. 26. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. 27. This drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: 28. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 29. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 30. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 31. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., some diabetic urine tests), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: 32. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. 33. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. 34. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Additional Notes: 35. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. 36. For long-term treatment, lab and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function, complete blood counts) should be conducted while taking this medication. 37. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: 38. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. 39. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Storage: 40. Store this medication in the refrigerator. 41. Discard any unused portion after 14 days, as the drug loses potency after this time. 42. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. 43. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Reminder: 44. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized information about this product and your health needs.
